newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Thousands flee Mobutu home region -- aid workers.
newsitem.headline: Thousands flee Mobutu home region -- aid workers.

text.p: Thousands of Zaireans, among them soldiers, have started fleeing ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko's home region into neighbouring Central African Republic, aid workers said, quoting witnesses.

The exodus, particularly in the region of Mobutu's former jungle palace at Gbadolite, began in earnest after the veteran strongman fled his capital for Gbadolite and Laurent Kabila's rebels entered the capital at the weekend, they added.
Mobutu later left Gbadolite for Togo, according to some reports fleeing advancing rebels.

Osseni Fasassi, representative of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees in the Central African Republic's capital Bangui, said he had reports of several thousand Zaireans arriving at Mobaye and Bangassou and other towns along the Ubangi River between the two nations.
Fassani last week persuaded the Central African Republic authorities to offer temporary refuge to 225 Rwandan Hutu refugees trapped in northern Zaire in fear of their lives.

He rejected suggestions by a Rwandan official on Saturday that armed Rwandan Hutus, who fought alongside Mobutu's defeated army and are blamed for Rwanda's 1994 genocide, were among those allowed across.
